correctness.rationale: On real 2x2 rank-one tangent plane T_W at W=e1e1^T, P_T deletes bottom-right entry. For a,b>0, g=[[a,b],[b,0]] is invertible symmetric indefinite and polar(g) is its sign matrix [[a,2b],[2b,-a]]/sqrt(a²+4b²). Iteration yields X_t=[[a,2^t b],[2^t b,0]]/sqrt(a²+4^t b²), all t≥1; the exact nuclear norm of g is sqrt(a²+4b²). Differentiation of the alignment in k=2^t proves strict decrease after t=1; factoring d/dy of squared alignment gives (k-2)^2(2ky-1)(2ky+1)/((1+k²y)^2(1+4y)^2), so the global minimum over y=b²/a²>0 at y=1/(2k) is 8k/(k+2)^2, with sharp alignment 2sqrt(2k)/(k+2). Independently factored derivative with symbolic algebra and evaluated fresh exact rational and polar examples; t=3 is 4/5 and t=5 is 8/17. The t=1 boundary is exactly 1. No spectral-norm feasibility or optimizer convergence failure is asserted.
